name: Spike Island
funding: £1.5M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £285k, Bristol City Council £30k, John James Foundation, Henry Moore Foundation, Pilgrim Trust, Ampersand, Art Fund; Hauser & Wirth partnership to 2028.
watch: An 80,000 sq ft production and exhibition space for contemporary art and design on Bristol's harbourside, with over 70 artist studios, fabrication workshops and non-commercial galleries.
why_flagged: £1.5M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £285k, Bristol City Council £30k, John James Foundation, Henry Moore Foundation, Pilgrim Trust, Ampersand, Art Fund; Hauser & Wirth partnership to 2028.
records_note: Names supporters by tier with no date and lists its trustees; no annual reports posted, accounts for 2021 to 2025 sit on the register.

name: State Hermitage Museum
watch: Hermitage Amsterdam cut ties on 3 March 2022. Canada sanctioned director Piotrovsky in 2023 and the EU listed him on 23 April 2026.
why_flagged: Its 2025 sponsor list includes VTB, Sberbank, Gazprom, Rosneft, Gazprom Neft and the Gazprombank foundation, plus Vladimir Potanin and his foundation. Potanin chairs the Board of Trustees.
records_note: The Hermitage posts yearly reports for 2009 to 2018 and a sponsor list by year (2022 seen); its reports name a board of trustees.

name: State Russian Museum
watch: Vladimir Gusev (director since 1988) moved to president in Feb 2023; Deputy Culture Minister Alla Manilova appointed director 25 Apr 2023. 3.61m visits in 2024 per TAN ranking.
why_flagged: Vladimir Gusev (director since 1988) moved to president in Feb 2023; Deputy Culture Minister Alla Manilova appointed director 25 Apr 2023. 3.61m visits in 2024 per TAN ranking.
records_note: The museum posts no annual report or accounts and no board; its partners page names VTB in text and shows other partners only as logos.

name: The State Tretyakov Gallery
funding: Federal Ministry of Culture budget, state-controlled banking sponsors.
watch: Director Zelfira Tregulova removed 9 Feb 2023 after a Ministry-forwarded complaint of 'destructive ideology' in the displays; Elena Pronicheva (daughter of an FSB general) replaced her; in Jan 2026 Olga Galaktionova (ex-ROSIZO, ex-Pushkin) took over. The Ministry cancelled the 9th Moscow Biennale at the New Tretyakov on 3 Nov 2022. The Gallery states 80+ companies and individuals support it.
why_flagged: Corporate partners include VTB, Sberbank, PSB, Gazprombank, Transneft, LUKOIL, Surgutneftegas and NOVATEK. Private patrons include Leonid Mikhelson and Alisher Usmanov; the V. Potanin Foundation also gives.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports (2015 to 2020 seen), fund reports to 2025, a named trustees list and a named thanks list for corporate supporters.

name: Stills
watch: Ended Baillie Gifford funding in June 2024.
why_flagged: Ended Baillie Gifford funding in June 2024.
records_note: It posts no annual reports, files accounts with the Scottish regulator, names 19 funders and supporters undated, and lists three board members.

name: Storm King Art Center
why_flagged: Bloomberg Philanthropies is listed in Storm King's 2025 donor list in the Ambassador tier ($100,000+).
records_note: It posts an income statement and balance sheet on its leadership page, names 2025 donors by tier, and lists its trustees, but no annual reports.

name: Sursock Museum
watch: Fondation Engie, a gas utility, is an energy sponsor.
why_flagged: Fondation Engie, a gas utility, is an energy sponsor.
records_note: Sursock posts its 2025 annual report, named supporter lists for 2024 to 2026, and its board of trustees, but no financial statements.

name: Tai Kwun
watch: Funded by the Hong Kong Jockey Club, a gambling operator.
why_flagged: Funded by the Hong Kong Jockey Club, a gambling operator.
records_note: Tai Kwun publishes no annual report or accounts; it names its Jockey Club funder and individual donors undated, and lists its company board.

name: Tanoto Art Foundation
watch: RGE (pulp, palm oil) includes Pacific Oil & Gas (unverified claim).
why_flagged: RGE (pulp, palm oil) includes Pacific Oil & Gas (unverified claim).
records_note: The foundation posts no annual report, accounts, donor list or board; its About page names only a curator, a communications manager and an adviser.

name: Tate Modern
funding: £120M (group). DCMS statutory grant-in-aid, Bank of America, Hyundai Motor, Uniqlo, philanthropic circles.
watch: Ended BP in 2016 after protests; Sackler name removed 2022.
why_flagged: Ended BP in 2016 after protests; Sackler name removed 2022.
records_note: Parent Tate posts accounts from 2010-11 to 2025-26 and annual reports, names supporters in its 2025-26 report, and lists its trustees.

name: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art (TMoCA)
funding: State museum owned by the arts deputy of Iran's Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance, which OFAC lists as an entity. The state set a 16.5 billion toman renovation budget.
watch: After 1979 the state kept its Western collection in storage. In 2017 the culture minister cancelled its Berlin and Rome loan show.
why_flagged: State museum owned by the arts deputy of Iran's Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance, which OFAC lists as an entity. The state set a 16.5 billion toman renovation budget.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; its site only names the Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance as the owner.

name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
funding: Paulson Family Foundation gave $15M in 2021 and the Eyal & Marilyn Ofer Family Foundation $5M in 2019.
watch: In September 2025 over 50 artists signed an open letter asking two exhibiting artists to cancel their show, citing Gaza. The director rejected cancelling exhibitions.
why_flagged: Paulson Family Foundation gave $15M in 2021 and the Eyal & Marilyn Ofer Family Foundation $5M in 2019. No sponsor list found on its site.
records_note: Its annual report link returns an error; it posts no accounts or donor list, and its trustees page names the board, undated.
